Internal notes / findings (first pass):

- Reproduced the loop using Hailey's HAR. The SAML assertion (NameID) being consumed by the portal contains the forwarded mailbox address (team+procure@hawthorne.com) while the invite token was minted for the original user (j.summers@hawthorne.com). The portal's session bind code rejects the mismatch and falls back to an interactive MFA enrollment flow, which in this case doesn't persist because the session cookie is scoped to the original token.
- Root cause appears to be the combination of: forwarded message altering the perceived principal + a missing claim we expect for persistent binding (urn:redwood:bind-to-token).

Immediate remediation options:
1) Reissue an invite bound to the team mailbox address (works but will create a shared account acceptance).
2) Reissue a one-time replacement invite with explicit binding param (preferred). I created a debug invite and attached re-sent packet for Ben to approve (hawthorne_invite_fixed.eml).
3) Engineering could add a fall-through that maps NameID aliases to invite recipients for a short window (requires ops changes and a rollback plan).

For now I recommend option #2 (fastest, audit-friendly). Ben — can you push the replacement invite and mark the previous token invalid? Hailey / IT: once you receive the new invite please open it in a private/incognito window and confirm you can complete MFA enrollment and see the dashboard.

Quoted for context:
> On 2026-08-23 09:12, Hailey Wells wrote:
